title: Pump-Free Microwave-Optical Bell Pair Generation for Teleportation-Based Quantum Transduction
authors: Fangxin Li, Jaesung Heo, Zhaoyou Wang, Benjamin Pingault, Xingyu Gao, Tengyang Ruan, Anjun Chu, David D. Awschalom, Andrew N. Cleland, Andrew P. Higginbotham, Alexander A. High, Liang Jiang
abstract: The coherent conversion between microwave and optical photons, known as quantum transduction, is critical for connecting superconducting processors to optical networks. Existing methods are limited by complications associated with optical pumping. We propose a pump-free microwave-optical Bell-pair source for teleportation-based transduction. Using a spin or atomic system resonantly coupled to optical and microwave cavities, the scheme generates loss-robust heralded Bell pairs. Across color centers, atomic ensembles, and phonon-mediated systems, this assembly achieves kilohertz-range heralding rates with high fidelity.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, pump-free method for generating microwave-optical Bell pairs, which is crucial for quantum transduction linking superconducting circuits to optical networks. By leveraging spin or atomic systems coupled to optical and microwave cavities, the authors demonstrate protocols that maintain high fidelity and operational rates while circumventing the noise issues associated with traditional optical pumping techniques.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving quantum transduction—the coherent conversion of quantum states between microwave and optical frequencies—while avoiding detrimental effects from strong optical pumping.
main_result: The authors propose and analyze a pump-free microwave-optical Bell-pair source (MO-NODE) that generates heralded Bell pairs using spin or atomic systems, achieving high fidelity and kilohertz-range rates.
method: The method involves engineering the entanglement generation via resonant coupling between a spin/atom system and microwave/optical cavities, utilizing time-bin encoding and cavity QED principles.
model_or_system: The work models three distinct physical implementations: single color centers, atomic ensembles (e.g., 87Rb), and phonon-mediated systems. The underlying physics is described using cavity QED Hamiltonians and decay rate analyses.
key_observables: Heralded Bell pair rate ($R_{	ext{herald}}$), heralded fidelity ($F_{	ext{herald}}$), and the dark-state leakage probability ($P_D|R$).
important_parameters: Cooperativity ($C$), cavity decay rates ($\kappa_o, \kappa_e$), spin dephasing time ($T_{2,s}$), and coupling strengths ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the critical-coupling limit, adiabatic elimination of cavity/phonon modes, and assuming the coupling rate exceeds intrinsic decoherence rates.
figures_summary: Figures compare direct transduction, teleportation-based transduction, and the proposed pump-free MO-NODE scheme across various physical platforms (spin, ensemble, phonon).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for pump-free transduction, detailing the single-spin protocol, generalizing to ensemble and phonon-mediated systems, and analyzing leakage probabilities in inhomogeneous environments.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental engineering challenge of quantum interconnects by providing detailed theoretical protocols for generating high-quality entangled pairs between microwave and optical domains using solid-state and atomic platforms.
